meta.title: Ex-Anthropic Whistleblower Suspects Chinese Spies Inside America’s AI Labs | PBD Podcast #868
meta.thread_line: 6 threads · why he quit and why 2027 is 'chaotic', China espionage and distillation, rebuttals to the 'fear porn' and regulatory-capture critics, Anthropic versus OpenAI culture and leadership, how the resignation tweet went viral, and the scenarios and personal prepping he'd plan for.

snapshot: Jacob Coxon, who spent three years on pre-training at OpenAI and Anthropic, resigned from Anthropic with a tweet (**803K likes, 175M views**) saying both labs are racing to self-improving superintelligence 'and gambling with our lives'.
His core call: **2027 will be 'chaotic'**; models will automate AI researchers' own work, and the crucial decisions on slowing down get made within the next couple of years.
He is ~**90% sure China already has spies at OpenAI and Anthropic**, wants security-clearance-style background checks, and says AI labs can hire foreign nationals where SpaceX cannot.
He rejects the 'fear porn' framings (regulatory capture, hype for the IPO): he forfeited unvested Anthropic equity (**seven figures**) and says he's libertarian everywhere except AI.

On the companies: Anthropic is a 'very aligned', mission-driven culture (seven co-founders, none left) led by an honest, paranoid Dario Amodei; OpenAI is more distracted; as an investor he would **'long Anthropic, definitely'**.
He says Anthropic could plausibly destroy OpenAI **by the end of the decade (~4 years)**, and that frontier AIs may be able to access bank accounts and government systems within **1-2 years**.
Personal prep he suggests: food, masks and basic supplies for a cyber attack, minor pandemic or civil unrest; he says AI-lab engineers are buying gold, guns and land.

themes.title: Why he quit: a 'super weapon' technology, a chaotic 2027, and a case for nationalizing
themes.lead: Coxon says AI models next year will automate much of everyone's work, most importantly AI researchers' own, and that private companies shouldn't hold the keys.
bullets: Resignation tweet from a fresh account (started January 2026) hit **803,000 likes and 175 million views**; he left after a week working on safety and then concluding 'there was no good plan'.
Prediction: AI will be in the news daily in 2027, 'like war in the background' in WWII; labs still treat it as normal business with dev days and product tweets.
He says it's a 'super weapon' that 'should be nationalized'; he's surprised Trump lets 'Dario Amodei and Sam Altman have the keys' — 'you wouldn't let Mark Zuckerberg have nukes'.
He says he doesn't demand nationalization, just that the seriousness warrants government control, plus vetting and background checks.

Trigger metric: the scary threshold is when AI can **automate its own development** (recursive self-improvement); extrapolation says that's likely in the next few years, after which labs stop releasing models publicly and it becomes a full race.
Models due in the next 3-4 months will be 'a lot better' at coding and automating his research; he can't give details, and he expects release-decision news stories.
He believes the crucial slow-down decisions will happen 'this decade' and within about the next two years.
Money left behind: 'seven figures' at Anthropic (unvested); he kept his OpenAI equity and is 'not going to milk this' — he expects a job predicting where AI goes.

quote.text: Whoever controls AI becomes a god.

themes.title: China already inside the labs: ~90% sure of spies, plus distillation and the cooperation case
themes.lead: Coxon argues a US slowdown can't be enforced against China unless labs are vetted, but that China's incentives are aligned enough to cooperate.
bullets: He is **90% sure** China has spies at OpenAI and Anthropic, based on staff joking about it and the absence of serious background checks; he won't name anyone.
Host asks about executives: he clears OpenAI's Mark Chen, Fidji Simo and Brad Lightcap and says most Chinese nationals are rank-and-file coders and researchers, not executives.
SpaceX 'can't hire Chinese nationals' (regulator), while AI labs can — he says restricting Chinese nationals 'will probably happen' and it's 'sad' because they're his friends.
Much of China's progress is **distillation**: logging into Claude and training models on the answers, so a US slowdown would also slow China.

Cooperation case: China's regime wouldn't want a destabilizing technology; incentives are aligned and a deal should be 'quite easy' — the host and he discuss a US-China AI 'red phone' and a Xi-Trump conversation.
Host's counter: China won't stop and won't allow inspections; Coxon says it depends on a deal's design and that stolen model weights could instantly create a 'real race'.
Third place in the race: he says the US and China are far ahead; the UK 'not at all' (that's why he's in the US).

quote.text: If they're not vetting for something that could be a super weapon technology, it's just crazy. It's like cowboy stuff.

themes.watch: The 90% figure is Coxon's personal estimate with no named evidence; he explicitly declines to name individuals.

names.name: SpaceX (SPCX)
names.blurb: Cited as an example of a company that cannot hire Chinese nationals.

themes.title: 'Fear porn'? Why a libertarian says the free market fails on AI safety
themes.lead: Host lists the skeptical readings; Coxon says he has nothing to gain, and that competition itself pushes labs to skip safety work.
bullets: Host's three 'fear porn' motives: a call for government control, Anthropic/OpenAI entrenching against competitors, and hyping an IPO ('you may 10x, 20x, 30x your money').
Coxon: he left in a personal capacity and has nothing to gain; fear-hyping may even hurt an IPO.

He agrees with Marc Andreessen and David Sacks about benefits but says their 'optimistic fast case is my slow case' and they 'haven't fully internalized how crazy it will get'; he thinks they'd agree once things get crazier.

He calls himself libertarian/pro-capitalism, pro nuclear power, pro deregulating drugs, biology research and 'human self-experimentation', and thinks the pandemic response was 'overblown' near the end.
Race logic: everyone chases power and wealth to be able to make change (OpenAI over fear of DeepMind, Anthropic over fear of OpenAI), so the market 'races off a cliff'.

Safety allocation: soon labs choose what **percentage of resources** goes to capability versus safety research ('like a video game', maybe 50-70%); he fears the market picks too low and wants a cross-lab and China agreement.

He says Elon Musk is himself scared of AI and only started xAI because others were building; roughly 30% of lab researchers are in their 20s, and he rejects a generic liberal-climate-fear explanation.

quote.text: My fast case looks like we have no control over it. We're just watching robots make themselves smarter every day.

themes.watch: Marc Andreessen and David Sacks are cited by the host as critics as holding the regulatory-capture view; Coxon rejects that charge for himself.

names.name: xAI
names.blurb: Coxon says Musk started it because others were building AI.

themes.title: Anthropic versus OpenAI: mission culture, Dario versus Sam, and who is ahead
themes.lead: Coxon says Anthropic is focused and unified, OpenAI is distracted, and he'd back Anthropic as an investor.
bullets: Anthropic has **seven co-founders, none of whom have left**; employees call themselves 'ants' and sacrifice for the mission; he left OpenAI ~four months ago and says it may have changed.
OpenAI built Sora and devices; he says Anthropic 'would never' since it's off the core path to superintelligence.
Dario Amodei is 'very honest', gives probabilities ('20% / 80%'), has a 'cult of personality'; Sam Altman has a 'reputation for dishonesty' and is vague about the future (armchair read, he says).
He says Amodei has animosity toward Altman and left OpenAI partly over not wanting Altman to control the technology; all seven Anthropic co-founders came from OpenAI.
Anthropic once promised never to overtake OpenAI; it now releases better models, which he attributes to competition and to the idea that being ahead buys time for safety.
**Could Anthropic destroy OpenAI?** Not today; by the **end of the decade (~4 years)**, 'quite plausibly yes' — the host likens the seven founders to a risk of a 'ruler, not a president'.
Investor view: 'as an investor I would long Anthropic, definitely'; the host mentions a $2 trillion IPO; he ranks Meta, Google and xAI behind and unsure of order.

Talent economics: a researcher reportedly got a ~$1B Meta package then joined Anthropic; Meta paid ~$250M for a 24-year-old; he says top researchers cut training-run costs of hundreds of millions and capex of hundreds of billions.

quote.text: Anthropic is very dangerous. It's a very aligned institution.

themes.watch: Coxon says his Dario/Sam characterizations are 'armchair psychology' and that he hasn't been at OpenAI for four months.

themes.title: The tweet: planned a week ahead, then exploded without a PR firm
themes.lead: Coxon says he copied Leopold Aschenbrenner's 'be strategic when you leave' approach but got a far larger response than expected.
bullets: He delayed quitting a week, briefed the **Wall Street Journal** (first big public Anthropic safety resignation) and asked a few outside friends to retweet.
Early boosters: AI-policy friends (e.g. Nathan Calvin at Encode); Anthropic's Evan Hubinger confirmed 'the people building this technology earnestly believe it could kill us all'.
Reply analysis the host cites: **43% agreed, 40% disagreed, 18% mixed**; he went from near zero to 300,000 followers in 48 hours.
Head of Anthropic pre-training Nick Joseph advised him to stay and influence from inside; Coxon agreed he was probably right but 'didn't want to be part of it'.

Musk retweeted agreeing he'd said this long ago and Coxon DM'd him; Musk had also called the thread possibly coordinated (caption garbled), which Coxon says was understandable given the account's size; Musk could check X and found it organic; Coxon regrets a spat tweet written sleep-deprived.

Smears he addresses: a past stay in a communist-leaning London house ('they hated me'), no meetings with Clinton or Sanders; he declined a Bannon-Sanders rally and has not answered politicians who reached out.
Background: read Nick Bostrom's Superintelligence at 15-16; two International Math Olympiad silver medals; joined OpenAI's residency at 23 when the company was ~300 people (now ~7,000-8,000); age 28.
He says nobody at OpenAI or Anthropic knew the thread was coming; peers joke that the company runs on AI (he asked Claude how to resign).

themes.title: Scenarios he plans for: hacked systems, a minor pandemic, unrest, and an AI that acts on its own
themes.lead: Coxon doesn't expect immediate apocalypse; he says the world becomes drone-and-robot-heavy and people should do basic prepping.
bullets: Capability timing: frontier AIs able to access bank accounts and government systems in his best guess **1-2 years**, with a Pentagon-network national-security risk already reported.
Biology: a lab or a person with AI help could release a 'not particularly dangerous' virus; red teamers jailbreak safeguards; he cites Anthropic blocking a possible bioweapon attempt.
Civil unrest: many employees expect to avoid public offices and relocate (Wyoming, North Dakota) if San Francisco turns dangerous for AI researchers.
Future world: drones bristling after Ukraine-Russia, robots, and decisions made by AI; 'if humans were the enemy, suddenly there's nothing we could do'.
Agent incident: the Hugging Face case, where AI agents (about 1,200 agents, ~70,000 messages per the host) attacked a site on their own idea.
Prep: food, masks, basic supplies for 'two-week' disruptions; he says lab engineers are buying **gold, guns and land**; he supports the Second Amendment though he doesn't own a gun.
Employees: 'everyone knows' they're building their replacement; Dario's *Machines of Loving Grace* essay implied Anthropic would take care of employees if replaced.

quote.text: Keeping the eyes open and seeing where things are going is the first step to action.

themes.watch: Several of these are scenarios he labels as possible, not predictions; the host supplies the Hugging Face figures from memory and says he could have them mixed up.

names.name: Gold
names.blurb: Coxon says lab engineers are buying gold, guns and land.

takeaways.title: Treat 2027 as the planning year for AI-driven change; test claims against model releases in the next 3-4 months.
Add background checks and access controls for anyone touching frontier-model code or weights.
Separate AI-lab fear talk from IPO incentives; Coxon himself says he'd long Anthropic.
Watch US-China AI 'red phone' talks and distillation controls, not just chip export rules.
Stock two weeks of food, masks and basics against cyber, pandemic or unrest scenarios.
Plan for white-collar automation: build skills and cash runway for a few years of uncertainty.

hot_takes.take: I'm 90% sure. It's almost certain that they have spies at OpenAI and Anthropic.
This is a super weapon technology that really should be nationalized.
In four years if Dario wanted to destroy OpenAI, he could. Quite plausibly, yes.
As an investor, I would long Anthropic. Definitely.
Sam has a reputation for dishonesty.
I think 2027 is going to be a crazy year.

claims.claim: 2027 will be a chaotic year driven by AI automating work and AI research.
Frontier AI can automate its own development within the next few years.
Anthropic could plausibly destroy OpenAI if it wanted to.
Frontier AI systems can access bank accounts and government systems.
The critical decisions on whether to slow AI development are made within the next couple of years.
Restrictions on Chinese nationals working at US AI labs will happen.
Models released in the next 3-4 months will be much better at coding and automating research.

other_news.title: A White House AI meeting included Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Greg Brockman (Altman was at OpenAI dev day); the host says the discussion followed the tweet's publicity.

Sources/people referenced: Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness, Nick Bostrom's Superintelligence, Dario Amodei's Machines of Loving Grace, Nick Joseph, Evan Hubinger, Nathan Calvin, Marc Andreessen, David Sacks, a US-China AI 'red phone' report, and an OpenAI whistleblower death (Coxon says he's sure it wasn't a hit and presumes suicide).
A reported OpenAI 'stuffed animal advisory council' for resolving conflict; Coxon hasn't seen it at the office.
A researcher's value: training runs cost hundreds of millions, so people with good 'taste' who fix bugs fast can justify billion-dollar packages.

glossary.def: Training one model on another model's answers, which Coxon says drives much of China's progress.
AI automating AI research so models improve themselves, the threshold Coxon finds scariest.
Deliberately attacking an AI system to find ways around its safeguards.
The large first phase of training a model, where Coxon worked at both labs.
